documents.title: Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: No single rule is set: "AI use must follow the instructions of the course and instructor", with "Unauthorized or misuse" subject to penalties and a citation duty when allowed. The decision is handed to instructors.
documents.summary: University-wide academic integrity guidance for AI. AI content is plagiarism unless the instructor authorizes it and it is cited; lists CES principles and faculty and student roles.

units.why: Sets the baseline expectation "complete their own work and demonstrate their own understanding" for all community members; this is ownership of submitted work (P29), not the explain-every-line rule P30.
units.anchor: expected to complete their own work and demonstrate their own understanding

units.why: "is considered a form of plagiarism" classifies unpermitted or uncited AI content as misconduct, so P36; it is not a concrete penalty (P37).
units.anchor: Using AI-generated content without permission or
units.frag_end: is considered a form of plagiarism.
units.policy: Using AI-generated content without permission or proper citation is considered a form of plagiarism.

units.why: "not to rely on AI tools to complete academic tasks unless clearly authorized by the course instructor" sets no AI unless authorized, the fallback rule P06; P19 is narrower (producing submitted work).
units.anchor: not to rely on AI tools to complete academic tasks unless clearly authorized

units.why: "AI use must follow the instructions of the course and instructor" hands the rule to each instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: AI use must follow the instructions of the course and instructor.

units.why: "If AI use is permitted, it must be properly cited" requires attribution of permitted AI use, P24; style details are a separate unit.
units.anchor: If AI use is permitted, it must be properly cited using an approved style

units.why: "may lead to academic penalties and disciplinary action" says unauthorized AI use or misuse is an integrity matter (P36); no specific penalty is named so not P37.
units.anchor: Unauthorized or misuse of Generative AI may lead to academic penalties and disciplinary action.

units.why: "you must cite them appropriately" when the instructor allows ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini or Claude is a citation requirement, P24.
units.anchor: you must cite them appropriately
units.frag_start: If your instructor allows the use

units.why: The university supplies an "AI Citation Style Guide" showing MLA, APA and Chicago formats; closest to P24 (not P25, since no required prompt or tool details are stated).
units.anchor: shows how to cite AI-generated content in MLA, APA, and Chicago formats
units.policy: BYU-Idaho publishes an AI Citation Style Guide showing how to cite AI-generated content in MLA, APA, and Chicago formats.

units.why: "protects you from unintentional plagiarism and shows academic honesty" explains that citing AI shields students from a plagiarism finding, which is how disclosure affects integrity (P28).
units.anchor: Citing AI tools protects you from unintentional plagiarism and shows academic honesty.

units.why: "ask your instructor or a librarian for help" with citing is a support channel; no type covers help-seeking about citation (P10 is about asking before using AI).
units.anchor: ask your instructor or a librarian for help
units.frag_start: If you're unsure how to cite
units.uncovered_note: Students unsure how to cite AI are told to ask the instructor or a librarian for help.

units.why: The university "encourages students to follow the CES AI Guiding Principles", an institution-level framework of principles for AI use, P56.
units.anchor: BYU–Idaho encourages students to follow the
units.policy: BYU-Idaho encourages students to follow the CES AI Guiding Principles.

units.why: "Use AI to support learning, not to shortcut it" gives the reason AI use is limited: shortcutting undermines learning, P41.
units.anchor: Use AI to support learning, not to shortcut it.

units.why: "Verify the accuracy of AI output" tells students to check AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Verify the accuracy of AI output.

units.why: "Never enter personal, private, or sensitive data into AI tools" is a data-protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: Never enter personal, private, or sensitive data into AI tools.

units.why: "Use only tools that are approved or well-vetted by the university" directs students to vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: tools that are approved
units.policy: Use only tools that are approved or well-vetted by the university.

units.why: "Always disclose when you use AI in your work" is a disclosure duty with each submission, P24.
units.anchor: Always disclose when you use AI in your work.

units.why: "Be honest about what you created and what AI generated" asks students to distinguish own from AI work in disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: Be honest about what you created and what AI generated.

units.why: "You are responsible for how you use AI" makes students accountable for their AI use, P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for how you use AI.

units.why: Students must "Follow the CES Honor Code, and Academic Integrity Policy", tying AI use to existing integrity rules, P36.
units.anchor: Follow the
units.policy: Students follow the CES Honor Code and Academic Integrity Policy in their AI use.

units.why: "When in doubt, ask" tells students unsure about a use to ask first, P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt, ask.

units.why: "Faculty should clearly define AI tool usage" asks instructors to state AI expectations, matching P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly define AI tool usage
units.policy: Faculty should clearly define AI tool usage.

units.why: Faculty should "model ethical AI" and "guide AI literacy", i.e. teach and demonstrate AI use, P44.
units.anchor: model ethical AI, ensure students grasp assignment purposes
units.policy: Faculty should model ethical AI and guide AI literacy.

units.why: Faculty should "ensure students grasp assignment purposes and demonstrate their own learning"; no type covers explaining assignment purpose, so UNCOVERED (not P41, which is about AI shortcutting practice).
units.anchor: ensure students grasp assignment purposes and demonstrate their own learning
units.uncovered_note: Faculty ensure students understand the purpose of assignments and demonstrate their own learning.

units.why: Faculty should "stay apprised of AI usage in the workforce, and align activities to prepare students for employment", a career-readiness expectation, P44.
units.anchor: align activities to prepare students for employment

units.why: "Students should follow the instructor's guidelines for AI use" defers to each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Students should follow the instructor’s guidelines for AI use
units.policy: Students follow the instructor's guidelines for AI use.

units.why: "seek to genuinely learn rather than shortcut the learning process" is the skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: seek to genuinely learn rather than shortcut the learning process
units.policy: Students seek to genuinely learn rather than shortcut the learning process.

units.why: "be transparent about when AI tools are used" is a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: be transparent about when AI tools are used
units.policy: Students are transparent about when AI tools are used.

units.why: "Students are responsible for ensuring their work reflects their own understanding and effort" is ownership of submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for ensuring their work reflects their own understanding and effort

units.why: The closing frames integrity as becoming "like our Savior Jesus Christ" and using AI responsibly as "part of that growth", a principle statement at institution level, P56.
units.anchor: Using AI responsibly is part of that growth.

documents.title: AI in the Syllabus
documents.stance_why: It says "Whether you allow full use or prohibit it entirely, the standard is to ensure students know exactly where your course stands", offering stoplight and scale tiers, so the stance is delegated with tiers.
tiers: AI Assessment Scale: No AI / AI for Ideas / AI for Feedback / AI for Content / AI-Led
documents.summary: Tells faculty every syllabus should carry a genAI statement and offers a wizard, two tier frameworks and resources to write it.

units.why: "Every course syllabus ... is expected to include a statement regarding the use of generative AI" requires an AI statement in each syllabus, P09.
units.anchor: expected to include a statement regarding the use of generative AI.

units.why: "Whether you allow full use or prohibit it entirely" leaves the stance to each instructor and only fixes that students must know it, so P04 rather than P09 (the statement duty is coded separately).
units.anchor: Whether you allow full use or prohibit it entirely
units.policy: Instructors may allow full use or prohibit AI entirely; the standard is that students know exactly where the course stands.

units.why: "Clear communication clarifies student expectations, promotes academic integrity, and models the transparency" is the rationale for the syllabus statement, P09.
units.anchor: Clear communication clarifies student expectations, promotes academic integrity

units.why: Bednar is quoted that technology "must not entice us to circumvent the struggle required for deep learning", the productive-struggle rationale, P41.
units.anchor: must not entice us to circumvent the struggle required for deep learning

units.why: "We use AI judiciously to help students become sound thinkers" states the institution's purpose for AI use, P56.
units.anchor: We use AI judiciously to help students become sound thinkers, skilled collaborators
units.frag_start: We use AI judiciously to help

units.why: The AI Statement Wizard helps instructors draft a syllabus statement, support for faculty in setting policy, P63.
units.anchor: AI Statement Wizard that will guide you through some thought exercises
units.frag_start: There is a BYU-Idaho AI Statement
units.frag_end: your preferred AI model to run this wizard:
units.policy: BYU-Idaho provides an AI Statement Wizard that guides instructors through thought exercises to draft a syllabus AI statement.

units.why: The Stoplight Framework names three levels (RED disallow, YELLOW limited, GREEN active), explicit tiers, P05.
units.anchor: Disallow. All work must be human-created.
units.frag_start: Select the model below that best
units.policy: The Stoplight Framework defines three levels: RED (disallow, all work human-created), YELLOW (limited use, specific tools permitted for defined tasks), GREEN (active application, intentional use of AI tools expected).

units.why: The AI Assessment Scale lists five levels from No AI to AI-Led, a second tier model, P05.
units.anchor: AI for Ideas
units.policy: The AI Assessment Scale defines five levels: No AI, AI for Ideas, AI for Feedback, AI for Content, and AI-Led.

units.why: A framework "to help them declare and reflect on their use of AI" asks students to declare and reflect, P26.
units.anchor: share with students to help them declare and reflect on their use of AI.
units.policy: Instructors can share a framework with students to help them declare and reflect on their use of AI.

units.why: A "style guide to share with students to help them cite their use of AI" supports citation, P24.
units.anchor: A style guide to share with students to help them cite their use of AI.
units.policy: Instructors can share a style guide with students to help them cite their use of AI.

units.why: The page offers a James Lang webinar to help faculty with integrity strategies, support for faculty, P63.
units.anchor: A webinar by author James Lang to help faculty learn more strategies
units.policy: A webinar helps faculty learn strategies for mitigating academic integrity problems related to AI.

documents.title: CSE Generative AI Usage Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy "encourages students to utilize AI tools for enhancing learning, creativity, and productivity" while "requiring them to disclose AI assistance", so encourage with conditions.
documents.summary: Department policy that encourages students to use generative AI for coding, learning and ideas, requiring a disclosure statement and IEEE-style citation on all work.

units.why: The policy "encourages students to utilize AI tools for enhancing learning, creativity, and productivity", a default of encouragement, P02.
units.anchor: encourages students to utilize AI tools for enhancing learning, creativity, and productivity

units.why: "integrate generative AI into the curriculum" states the department aim of building AI into courses, P44.
units.anchor: aims to integrate generative AI into the curriculum
units.policy: This policy aims to integrate generative AI into the curriculum.

units.why: Students are encouraged to "Explore and use generative AI tools to assist with coding tasks", allowing AI-assisted code; P16 (AI code allowed with conditions, here disclosure) fits better than P02, the overall default.
units.anchor: Explore and use generative AI tools to assist with coding tasks

units.why: "the same collaborative spirit as pair programming, tutoring sessions" compares AI to a human collaborator, P45.
units.anchor: same collaborative spirit as pair programming, tutoring sessions, or one-on-one meetings with professors

units.why: "Use generative AI as a learning resource to understand different approaches" is AI for understanding concepts, P12.
units.anchor: Use generative AI as a learning resource to understand different approaches to coding

units.why: "streamline repetitive and time-consuming tasks strategically" permits AI to automate routine work; closest is P16 (AI doing coding work), same type as the coding-tasks unit.
units.anchor: streamline repetitive and time-consuming tasks strategically

units.why: "Maintain an active role in decision-making throughout the automation process" keeps the student as decision-maker, P32.
units.anchor: Maintain an active role in decision-making throughout the automation process.

units.why: "code completion, debugging, and optimization" are listed as encouraged uses; debugging is the headline use so P13.
units.anchor: Use generative AI tools for code completion, debugging, and optimization

units.why: "a source of inspiration to explore novel ideas" is brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: Use generative AI as a source of inspiration to explore novel ideas

units.why: "generate diverse perspectives and approaches" is exploring alternative approaches, P15.
units.anchor: generate diverse perspectives and approaches to software development challenges

units.why: "as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, personal learning efforts" keeps AI from replacing the student's thinking, P32.
units.anchor: as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, personal learning efforts
units.frag_start: Embrace generative AI as a tool

units.why: "Utilize the AI for self-reflection, identifying areas for improvement" is AI for self-checks of knowledge, P14.
units.anchor: Utilize the AI for self-reflection, identifying areas for improvement
units.frag_start: Embrace generative AI as a tool

units.why: "A statement indicating that AI was used ... is required in all works" requires disclosure with each submission, P24.
units.anchor: AI was used to aid in its production is required in all works.

units.why: The IEEE example gives tool, vendor, date and URL, so it states what a citation includes, P25.
units.anchor: Text generated by ChatGPT, OpenAI, March 7, 2023, https://chat.openai.com/chat.
units.policy: AI citations follow IEEE format, naming the tool, vendor, date and URL, e.g. "Text generated by ChatGPT, OpenAI, March 7, 2023, https://chat.openai.com/chat."

units.why: "students should indicate what and where these portions are" marks which parts are AI-assisted and which not, locating AI use in the work, P27.
units.anchor: students should indicate what and where these portions are in the work
units.frag_start: If some portions of the work

units.why: "Personal involvement should be a constant" keeps the student the active problem-solver, P32.
units.anchor: Personal involvement should be a constant as you use these tools
units.frag_start: Treat generative AI as a supplementary

units.why: Integration "supports the development of proficient and ethical software developers", a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: supports the development of proficient and ethical software developers
units.frag_start: Integrating generative AI into the department
